mira: Heads up — after yesterday's continuous-batching tweak I'm seeing a regression for streaming responses. p50 went ~40ms -> ~80ms, p99 ~250ms -> ~420ms on canary. It looks like partial-decode is waiting for token_budget before the first frame is emitted. Logs show kernel_switch spikes during batch formation. Anyone else?

sam: saw similar on canary, +1. Partial-decode scheduler delaying first byte. KV cache hit rate looks fine so not a cold-cache issue. Flamegraph attached in thread (snippet below). :eyes:

kevin: my first guess is queue ordering. Small streaming replies are getting queued behind big estimated-token requests because our token_budget_target encourages fuller batches. We may need a short-job-first bias for streaming or preemptive flush.

anya: agree. Quick idea: treat streaming requests as "latency-first" and allow them to preempt batch formation after X ms or on first token. Something like:

```
"batch_policy": {
  "mode": "continuous",
  "token_budget_target": 80,
  "max_batch_tokens": 256,
  "stream_flush_on_first_token": true,
  "queue_strategy": "size-biased" // prefer requests with small estimated remaining
}
```

sam: also worth tuning kernel selection hints. For short seqs we can pick the low-latency kernel variant (smaller block size / less quant-decode overhead) to reduce kernel-switch amortization. Maybe add kernel_warm_hint when KV cache hits>0 so we avoid eviction thrash on kernel handoff.

mira: tried enabling stream_flush_on_first_token=true on a dev pod and re-ran the perf job. p50 ~35ms, p99 ~140ms. Good latency win but throughput/regression: cost up ~6% because batching less effectively. So we need a hybrid approach.

kevin: what about changing partial_decode_granularity from 32-token frames to 8-token frames for the first 64 tokens, then grow frame size after warmup. Smaller frames give faster first byte but increase kernel call frequency. Rough math: extra kernel invocations add ~6–10us each on this hw.

anya: propose adaptive granularity + opportunistic SJF:
- for streaming requests, if estimated_response_tokens <= 64 -> high priority
- otherwise allow them to join normal batch unless waiting > T_flush_ms
- adaptive_frame_sizes = [8, 16, 32] for first/next/subsequent chunks

perf-bot: perf-run 2024-04-02T12:10Z: baseline(p99 streaming) = 420ms, preemptive-flush config = 140ms, end-to-end throughput -5%. Full traces: s3://redwood-perf/canary/2024-04-02/trace.tar.gz

sam: i'll prototype an "opportunistic-sjf" scheduler flag that reorders the queue by estimated_remaining_tokens for streaming requests and emits preemptive flushes if first_token_wait > 8ms. Need a simple estimator: est_remaining = max(1, ceil((prompt_tokens + expected_response_tokens)/16)).

mira: also observed KV cache evictions when we switch kernel_variant mid-request — KV page refs get pinned to kernel memory. We should either pin KV across compatible kernels or implement a cheap migrate-kv path to avoid cold-starting the KV slice on a kernel switch. Filing a follow-up infra ticket.

kevin: opened a tiny PR with the scheduler flag + unit tests (DRAFT): https://git.redwood/internal/pr/2345. Test driver attached that simulates mixed short/long streaming traffic.

anya: can someone run an overnight canary with opportunistic-sjf + kernel_hint + adaptive_frame_sizes? i'll collect traces and perf counters for p50/p95/p99 and token-cost delta. If results look good we'll roll to staged tomorrow. :+1:

sam: i'll run it tonight on two canary pods and post results by morning.

mira: thanks — appreciate the quick follow-up. If the canary looks stable, let's add a telemetry tag so we can split metrics by: preemptive_flush=true, queue_strategy=opportunistic-sjf, kernel_hint=enabled.

kevin: noted. will include telemetry flags.
